{{nihongo|'''Izanagi Jingū'''|伊弉諾神宮}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Awaji Province]].

[[File:Izanagi-jingu, otorii-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Otorii}}]]'''Izanagi Jingu'' (Izanagi Jingu) is located in {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}{{ill|Awaji, Hyōgo|Q373107|qid=Q373107}} Taga. {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}), {{ill|Awaji Province|Q1053717|qid=Q1053717}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}}. {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{ill|Q712534|lt=Kanpei Taisha}}, and currently it is {{ill|Beppyo shrine|ja|別表神社|mr|बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|simple|Beppyo shrine|zh|別表神社|qid=Q10898274}} of {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}.The name of the former location, {{ill|Ichinomiya, Hyōgo (Tsuna)|Q5986243|qid=Q5986243|lt=Ichinomiya Town}} (currently Awaji City), originates from our company. Commonly known as ``Ikku-san'' and ``Izanou-san.'' On {{ill|January 15|Q2260|qid=Q2260}} ({{ill|koshōgatsu|Q137803901|qid=Q137803901}}), the Awaji Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries Festival will be held in addition to the Ogayu Fortune Festival. {{ill|2016|Q25245|qid=Q25245}}{{ill|April 25|Q2531|qid=Q2531}} was certified as {{ill|Japan Heritage|Q18382798|qid=Q18382798}} as one of the constituent cultural properties<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story030/ |title=STORY #030 “Awaji, the island of national birth” that decorates the beginning of “Kojiki” - The activities of the mariners who supported the ancient nation - |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=2020-08-04 }}</ref>.

=== Enshrined God ===
* {{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami Mikoto}}

Both gods appear in the Japanese mythology {{ill|Kuniumi|Q3545163|qid=Q3545163}} and {{ill|Kamiumi|Q3545159|qid=Q3545159}}.Since the enshrined deity in "Yukyu Goki" is "Izanagi no Ichibushira," it is thought that originally only Izanagi was enshrined. </ref>. {{ill|1931|Q18782|qid=Q18782}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|ar|فترة شووا|br|Oadvezh Shōwa|ca|Període Shōwa|cs|Období Šówa|de|Shōwa-Zeit|eo|Ŝova-epoko|es|Era Shōwa|eu|Shōwa aroa|fa|دوره شووا|fi|Shōwa-kausi|fr|Ère Shōwa (1926-1989)|he|תקופת שווה|hi|शोवा युग|hu|Sóva-kor|id|Zaman Shōwa|it|Periodo Shōwa|ja|昭和|ka|შოვას პერიოდი|ko|쇼와 시대|lt|Šiova laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Shōwa|nl|Showaperiode|no|Shōwa-perioden|pl|Shōwa|pt|Período Shōwa|ru|Сёва|simple|Shōwa era|sr|Шова период|sv|Shōwa|th|ยุคโชวะ|tl|Panahong Shōwa|tr|Şova Dönemi|uk|Період Сьова|vi|Thời kỳ Chiêu Hòa|zh|昭和|zh_classical|昭和|zh_min_nan|Chiau-hô|zh_yue|昭和|qid=Q327567}}6) "Ancient Shrine Document Copy" contains a petition regarding the enshrined deity, which states, The shrine is also of the highest rank, and the status of the shrine is Kanpei Taisha.The two deities, Izanami no Mikoto and Izanami no Mikoto, were born domestically and divinely, and these two deities should be enshrined regardless of the number of shrines listed in "{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}." |Q3125096}} In {{ill|1870|Q7741|qid=Q7741}}, {{ill|Myōdō Prefecture|Q9610752|qid=Q9610752}} designated Izanagi as the sole pillar. This is unfair as the subsidiary shrine of the Sesha was officially recognized. }} (1932) When we opened the main shrine, we found that Izami no Mikoto was also being enshrined as it had been handed down, so we requested permission to enshrine the two deities, Izanakomiko and Izami no Mikoto, with the request along with some materials, and {{ill|1932|Q18743|qid=Q18743}} (Showa 7) {{ill|Minister of Home Affairs|Q11267748|qid=Q11267748|lt=Minister of the Interior}} ``We have received permission to increase the number of enshrined deities,'' and the shrine officially began to enshrine two deities<ref name="kamigami" />.In addition, {{ill|Takeshi Matsumae|Q11529297|qid=Q11529297}} argues that the myth of the local god Izanagi was incorporated into the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yamato Court}} mythology from Awaji Province.<ref name="matsumae">From Ken Matsumae, "Japanese Gods," Chuokoronsha Co., Ltd., September 1974. </ref>. According to Matsumae, it does not seem that the belief that Izana no Mikoto was the parent of the Imperial Ancestor God existed in the imperial court for a long time; the two gods were only incorporated after the mid-seventh century, and it was passed down by people from Awaji who were called to {{ill|Daijosai|Q11433653|qid=Q11433653}} rituals for Rabbit's Day, and by Awaji seamen who brought food to the imperial court.<ref name="matsumae" /> Furthermore, in ``{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}'', it is said that the reason why our company jumped from the 8th rank of Muppin to the highest rank of Ippin is that it was during this period that he was officially made the next relative of the Imperial Ancestor God.<ref name="matsumae" />

=== History ===

=== Founding ===
In ``{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}'' and ``{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}},'' it is said that Izanagi no Mikoto, who had finished domestic and divine births, rested in a mysterious palace (kakurinomiya, final abode) in Taga, the land where he first gave birth, {{ill|Awaji Island|ar|أواجي (جزيرة)|az|Avaci adası|bcl|Isla nin Awaji|be|Авадзі (востраў)|bg|Аваджи (остров)|bn|আয়াজি দ্বীপ|ca|Illa d'Awaji|ceb|Awaji Shima|cs|Awadži|da|Avaji|de|Awaji-shima|el|Αβάτζι|eo|Aŭaĝi|es|Isla Awaji|et|Awaji saar|eu|Awaji uhartea|fa|جزیره آواجی|fi|Awaji|fr|Awaji-shima|gl|Illa de Awaji|he|אוואג'י (אי)|hi|अवाजी द्वीप|hy|Ավաձի (կղզի)|id|Pulau Awaji|it|Isola Awaji|ja|淡路島|ko|아와지섬|la|Insula Awaji|lb|Awaji-shima|lt|Avadžis|nl|Awaji (eiland)|pl|Awaji (wyspa)|pt|Ilha Awaji|ro|Insula Awaji|ru|Авадзи (остров)|sl|Avadži (otok)|sv|Awaji|tg|Ҷазираи Авадзӣ|th|เกาะอาวาจิ|tr|Awaji Adası|uk|Авадзі|vi|Awaji (đảo)|wuu|淡路岛|zh|淡路島|qid=Q504373}}, which is said to be the origin of our company. The other place that is said to be the ghost shrine of Izanagison is {{jalink|Taga Taisha|Q402091} in {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Shiga|af|Shiga-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Shiga|ar|شيغا (محافظة)|az|Şiqa prefekturası|azb|شیقا اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Shiga|be|Сіга (прэфектура)|bg|Шига|bn|শিগা প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|br|Prefedelezh Shiga|ca|Prefectura de Shiga|cdo|Shiga-gâing|ce|Сига (префектура)|ceb|Shiga-ken|ckb|پارێزگای شیگا|cs|Prefektura Šiga|cy|Shiga (talaith)|da|Shiga-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Shiga|eo|Gubernio Ŝiga|es|Prefectura de Shiga|et|Shiga prefektuur|eu|Shiga (prefektura)|fa|استان شیگا|fi|Shigan prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Shiga|frr|Shiga (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Shiga|gl|Prefectura de Shiga|hak|Shiga-yen|he|שיגה (מחוז)|hr|Shiga (prefektura)|hu|Siga prefektúra|hy|Սիգա (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Shiga|ilo|Prepektura ti Shiga|it|Prefettura di Shiga|ja|滋賀県|jv|Préfèktur Shiga|ka|სიგის პრეფექტურა|ko|시가현|la|Shigaënsis|lt|Šigos prefektūra|lv|Sigas prefektūra|mk|Шига (префектура)|mn|Шига муж|mni|ꯁꯤꯒꯥ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|शिगा प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Shiga|ne|सिगा|nl|Shiga (prefectuur)|no|Shiga (prefektur)|os|Сигæ|pl|Prefektura Shiga|pnb|ضلع شیگا|pt|Shiga|ro|Prefectura Shiga|ru|Сига|sco|Shiga Prefectur|se|Shiga prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Shiga|si|ෂිගා ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Shiga Prefecture|sk|Šiga (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Шига|su|Préféktur Shiga|sv|Shiga prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Shiga|tg|Устони Шига|th|จังหวัดชิงะ|tl|Prepektura ng Shiga|tr|Shiga|tt|Сига (префектура)|uk|Префектура Сіґа|ur|شیگا پریفیکچر|vi|Shiga|war|Shiga (prefektura)|wuu|滋贺县|zh|滋贺县|zh_classical|滋賀縣|zh_min_nan|Siga-koān|zh_yue|滋賀縣|qid=Q131358}} }, which is written in the Shinpuku-ji book of Kojiki, ``The late Izanagi Ōkamija za'''tankai'''no'''Taga'''ya.'' (Izanagi no Okami is According to the description of ``Afumi no Tagani Masanari''. However, it is known that the deity enshrined at Taga Taisha Shrine was not Izanagison until the period of the Northern and Southern Courts, so it is not possible to connect the description in the Kojiki with Taga Taisha Shrine. In the Kojiki, ``Omi'' is usually referred to as ``Kindankai,'' and even in the same ``Kojiki,'' many manuscripts other than the Shinpukuji version refer to ``the late Iyanagi Daishinshaza''''Awaji''''. 'Taga'''ya.', and for various other reasons, there is a prevailing theory in academic circles that supports 'Awaji' rather than 'Awami' (Yukichi Takeda, Kojiro Naoki, etc.). Furthermore, in "Nihonshoki" it is consistently written as "Awaji", and there is no name that corresponds to "Omi".

=== Outline ===

(Japan)|Q1143910|Koji}} was converted to {{ill|Nichiren-shū|Q206611|qid=Q206611}} by Mr. Tamura in the first year ({{ill|1555|Q6579|qid=Q6579}}), and {{jali nk|Genroku|Q1325001}} From the description in ``A copy of the reply letter with an addendum from the priest of the temple priest'' dated August 12 ({{ill|1699|Q7710|qid=Q7710}}), it is known that shrine priests who did not comply with the conversion were expelled. For this reason, there is a theory that the Tamura clan had jurisdiction over Ichinomiya at the end of the medieval period<ref name="kiso" />.In {{ill|1870|Q7741|qid=Q7741}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}3), {{ill|Myōdō Prefecture|Q9610752|qid=Q9610752}} decided to enshrine one deity, Izanagison, instead of two. In {{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}} (Meiji 4), it was promoted to Kokuhei-chusha, and in {{ill|1885|Q7821|qid=Q7821}} (Meiji 18), it was promoted to {{ill|Q712534|lt=Kanpei Taisha}}. {{ill|1995|Q2068|qid=Q2068}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}}7) It suffered significant damage, including the collapse of the first torii gate in the {{ill|Damage by Great Hanshin earthquake|Q11392882|qid=Q11392882}} of {{ill|January 17|Q2264|qid=Q2264}}. The torii gate was rebuilt in November of the same year, with the format changed to {{ill|Torii|Q234731|qid=Q234731|lt=Shinmei Torii}}, with the dedication of {{ill|Ujiko|Q125562175|qid=Q125562175}}.

There is a {{ill|fragrant wood|Q87216239|qid=Q87216239}} stone monument in the precincts.

* Settsu Shrine/Kama Shrine - Guardian deity of sake brewing and brewing. <ref name=":0" /> is worshiped as the god of warding off disaster and fire protection.
* Iwakusu Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|Hiruko|Q1067028|qid=Q1067028|lt=Ebisu no Mikoto}}. It is enshrined at the base of a large camphor tree (designated by Hyogo Prefecture as a natural monument) that is approximately 900 years old. It is said to be the god of childbirth and safe childbirth. It has been enshrined since the middle of the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}.
